verdict.rationale: Grafana's evidence shows only recurring evaluation of user-defined rules: alert rules are continuously evaluated and send notifications to Slack, PagerDuty and similar tools, and Mimir supports recording rules that periodically generate new data. That amounts to built-in recurring automation, but not general-purpose scheduling of arbitrary jobs or workflows. The 'on-call schedules' evidence covers staff rotations, not job scheduling. Missing for 10: a general job/workflow scheduler with cron-style or interval configuration, scheduled reports or exports, documentation of evaluation-interval control, and independent or hands-on corroboration of scheduling workflows.
